ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs and directors against FINTRAC guidance on politically exposed persons (PEPs), Global Affairs Canada sanctions lists under the Special Economic Measures Act, United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, and OFAC SDN List. Enhanced due diligence required for any PEP, foreign PEP, or person resident in or connected to sanctioned jurisdictions. All screening results must be documented and retained in the corporate records register.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (online filing through authorized registry agents; NUANS name search and reservation via Corporate Registry system)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be in English or French using Latin script, with permitted punctuation and numerals. There is no mandatory transliteration from other scripts, but any name registered must be represented in Latin characters on the NUANS report and Alberta corporate registry. The name must be distinct and not confusing with existing names under ABCA s. 10(2), and a NUANS pre-search report is required for every proposed corporate name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A NUANS report is valid for 90 days; if incorporation is not completed within that window, a new search and reservation must be filed. If a name is rejected, the applicant may either file a revised name through a registry agent or submit a written appeal to the Registrar of Companies within 30 days of rejection, stating the grounds of distinctiveness and compliance. The Registrar may hold an administrative review; further judicial review is available at the Court of King's Bench of Alberta.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible. An Alberta unlimited liability corporation must maintain a registered office address in Alberta that is a physical location capable of accepting service of process. Virtual office providers offering a dedicated street address, mail handling, and registered agent service are accepted. A post office box alone is not permitted. For this LegalTech SaaS operation, the physical presence requirement is minimal and virtual office use is consistent with standard administrative practice.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: est. below 5% for a non-licensed, low-risk cloud software entity; however, unannounced physical inspection may occur at the registered office for verification of corporate register maintenance, tax audit, or AML/CFT compliance review.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9, as amended, particularly ss. 9-12 (incorporation and articles), s. 15 (registered office), ss. 101-106 (directors and officers), and the regulations thereunder.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporate Registry, Service Alberta, Government of Alberta, acting through accredited service providers on the Alberta Corporate Registry platform.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation filed electronically via the Alberta Corporate Registry by an accredited service provider, accompanied by the Initial Notice of Registered Office and statutory fee payment.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is required under the Alberta Business Corporations Act for an unlimited liability corporation; no escrow account is required at incorporation. Shares may be subscribed and issued for such lawful consideration as fixed by the board of directors.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Corporation be incorporated under the Alberta Business Corporations Act as an unlimited liability corporation and that its articles of incorporation filed with the Corporate Registry be ratified. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Corporation validly issue its initial common shares to the founding subscribers for the consideration fixed by the board and recorded in the share subscription ledger. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office be [address], Alberta, and that [firm] be appointed registered agent. FURTHER RESOLVED, that [President], [Treasurer], and [Secretary] be appointed Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, and Corporate Secretary, respectively, to serve until the next board resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Corporate Name Search and Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (through authorized NUANS channel)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS corporate name search request through an accredited service provider. Verify availability of the proposed name and its compliance with the corporate name regulations. If required, file a name reservation to protect the selected ULC name on the Alberta Corporate Registry.
required_dossiers: Proposed articles information including name, jurisdiction and entity type
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name search reveals a conflict or the registry issues a name objection, select an alternative corporate name and resubmit the NUANS report, or file a written response with legal arguments to the Registry for reconsideration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Filing of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (electronic filing through accredited service provider)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and execute the Articles of Incorporation, including the unlimited liability designation, share structure, registered office address, initial directors, and authorized restrictions. Submit the executed articles and supporting consents electronically, pay the statutory filing fee, and obtain the Certificate of Incorporation after approval.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as director for each initial director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a query or rejection, correct the deficient articles and refile through the same channel; if the certificate is issued with an error, request a correction or amendment filing and pay the applicable remedial fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment of Registered Office and Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Registry, Service Alberta / appointed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Notice of Registered Office and maintain a registered office at a physical address in Alberta acceptable to the Registry and open for document service during normal business hours. Create the statutory corporate records book, including articles, by-laws, minutes, share register, and directors register.
required_dossiers: Consent of registered office occupant or lease evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered office is queried or returned, provide corrected location documentation or file an Address Change Notice; if the registered agent fails to accept service, appoint a replacement agent and update the Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Meeting and First Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors / subscribers of the corporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene an organizational meeting of the incorporators or initial directors to adopt the first board resolution approving the issuance of shares to subscribers, appointing officers, approving the registered office and corporate records, and ratifying the articles of incorporation. Record formal minutes in the corporate minute book.
required_dossiers: Call of organizational meeting and consent to act
Waiver of notice and meeting minutes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a procedural defect is identified, cure it by unanimous written consent resolution signed by all directors or shareholders, as applicable, and insert the curative resolution in the corporate records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Share Subscription, Issuance and Capitalization Ledger
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Record the share subscriptions of the founding shareholders, determine the consideration for the initial common shares, issue share certificates reflecting the unlimited liability nature of the corporation, and enter all issuances in the share register and members' ledger.
required_dossiers: Share certificate stubs and countersigned certificates
Resolution of the board fixing the issue price
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a subscription is incomplete or consideration is unpaid, require a revised subscription agreement or obtain a board resolution preserving other claims; reissue corrected certificates upon surrender of prior certificates.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Initial Annual Return and Director Information Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 60 days after incorporation, prepare and file the Initial Annual Return with the Corporate Registry. Provide current director information, registered office address and corporate status details using the secure electronic filing system.
required_dossiers: Notice of change of directors if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the return is rejected for incomplete data, amend and resubmit immediately; if the filing deadline is missed, file a late return and pay the applicable late-filing penalty before enforcement action is taken.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Governance By-Laws and Statutory Records Completion
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt general operating by-laws governing meetings, quorum, officers, issuance and transfer of shares, indemnification and financial authority. Ensure all governance records are permanently stored at the registered office and remain available for inspection by members and regulators.
required_dossiers: Minutes of the first directors meeting adopting the by-laws
Governance policies and internal controls checklist
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If by-law adoption is challenged or omitted, call a special directors meeting to ratify the by-laws by resolution and document the ratification in the corporate minute book.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No physical operating licence or manufacturing permit required; the company is not subject to Alberta's industrial licensing regime for its computing, cloud document automation, and e-signature activities.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas for EIA; municipal utility authorities for general discharge approvals
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Not triggered - office-based software technology services fall outside mandatory EIA classes under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act and do not involve a physical works project.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No point-source wastewater discharge, VOC emissions, or hazardous waste streams are generated. Compliance with municipal sewer and solid waste bylaws and general workplace OHS ventilation standards is sufficient.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification and workplace occupancy clearance for the Alberta registered office are required under the Alberta Fire Code and Alberta Occupational Health and Safety Act. national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC). National registration and filing portals: Business Registration Online (BRO) and My Business Account (MyBA) at canada.ca. The Alberta provincial corporate income tax is administered and collected by the CRA under the Canada-Alberta Tax Collection Agreement, so no separate provincial tax registration is required; incorporation is effected separately through the Alberta Corporate Registry (OneStep).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the Alberta Unlimited Liability Corporation (ULC) under the Alberta Business Corporations Act (ABCA) through the Alberta Corporate Registry; no minimum capital contribution is required and non-resident shareholders are permitted. Step 2: Register the corporation with the CRA via Business Registration Online (BRO) using the legal name and corporate registry number; the CRA issues the nine-digit Business Number (BN), which is the statutory tax identifier (functional equivalent of a TIN/VAT ID) for all federal and Alberta tax obligations. Step 3: Open the required CRA program accounts under the BN: corporate income tax (T2), GST/HST (program account suffix RT), payroll (suffix RP) if employees are engaged, and import/export accounts if goods are physically moved. Step 4: Because Alberta corporate income tax is collected by the CRA, the provincial tax is computed and reported as part of the single federal T2 corporate income tax return; no separate Alberta account is opened. Step 5: Register for GST/HST before making the first taxable supply if worldwide taxable revenues exceed the CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold; voluntary registration below the threshold is available and is commercially advisable for a LegalTech SaaS exporter because it permits input tax credit recovery and zero-rated export refund claims. The BN must be printed on every GST/HST invoice.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The Alberta ULC is Pass_Through_Eligible solely through the U.S. check-the-box regime: a U.S. shareholder files IRS Form 8832 (Entity Classification Election) within 75 days of formation, with late-election relief available, to classify the ULC as a disregarded entity or partnership for U.S. federal income tax purposes. The resulting structure is a hybrid entity: Canadian domestic law contains no analogue election, and the CRA treats the ULC as a taxable Canadian corporation subject to entity-level federal Part I tax and Alberta corporate income tax, so the ULC files its own T2 return. Ancillary statutory elections include: (i) the closely-related registrants election under Excise Tax Act (ETA) s. 156, which can deem taxable intercorporate supplies between the ULC and qualifying affiliates to be for nil consideration, eliminating GST/HST on intra-group SaaS and IT cost-recharge invoices; and (ii) alignment with Canada's hybrid-mismatch rules (Income Tax Act ss. 18.4-18.5) and Canada-United States tax treaty tie-breaker and limitation-on-benefits provisions, which CRA may invoke to deny deductions or recharacterize payments where the check-the-box outcome creates deduction/non-inclusion mismatches.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification_note: Despite the Pass_Through_Eligible designation, the Canadian domestic default is Entity_Level_Taxation; the pass-through outcome exists only for U.S.-side shareholders that elect check-the-box treatment and has no effect on CRA-assessed liability.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms_note: The ULC cannot elect entity-level pass-through status inside Canada; the CRA will assess the ULC as a corporation even when the sole shareholder is a U.S. person that has filed a Form 8832 disregarded-entity election.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop_note: The BN is the single identifier for GST/HST, corporate income tax, payroll, and customs; a non-resident ULC shareholder does not replace the corporation's BN with a personal tax number for GST/HST purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.indirect_tax_system_name_note: GST/HST is a federal VAT imposed under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act; because Alberta is not a harmonized province and imposes no provincial retail sales tax, only the 5% federal GST rate applies in Alberta.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules_note: The ULC, being incorporated in Alberta and resident in Canada, is subject to GST/HST on all taxable supplies made in Canada; a LegalTech SaaS provider making supplies to Canadian customers must charge 5% GST on each invoice and remit net tax on the GST/HST return.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not operate a mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or tax-authority API validation regime; the Pan-Canadian E-Invoice network, based on the OECD/Peppol framework, is being introduced on a voluntary basis for B2B interoperability, and CRA accepts commercial electronic invoices in PDF, XML, or UBL format without pre-clearance.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) designated as the Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act (Canada); in Alberta only the federal component applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 worldwide taxable supplies made in the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters (the ETA s. 148 small-supplier threshold); registration is mandatory once exceeded, and a non-resident supplier of digital services to Canadian consumers is deemed to carry on business in Canada and must register at the same CAD 30,000 threshold. Voluntary registration is available below the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, no digital stamping, and no continuous transaction control (CTC) API filing regime applies in Canada. The Pan-Canadian E-Invoice network (voluntary Peppol/UBL-BIS standard) is being piloted by the federal government for B2B interoperability. CRA accepts paper or common electronic invoice formats. Registrants whose total annual taxable supplies exceed CAD 1,500,000 must file GST/HST returns electronically (GST/HST NETFILE or a certified service provider), and registrants with annual net tax remittances above CAD 50,000 must remit electronically. A valid GST/HST invoice must show the supplier name, the 9-digit Business Number, the date of supply, a description, the consideration, the GST amount charged or a 'tax included' statement, and, where the recipient is a registrant, the recipient's BN and GST/HST registration status.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name_note: GST/HST is imposed at the federal level; Alberta has no provincial sales tax and no HST component, making Alberta a tax-effective jurisdiction for SaaS and digital services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.standard_headline_rate_percentage_note: The 5% Alberta GST rate applies to taxable supplies made in Canada; exports to non-residents are zero-rated at 0% where the statutory conditions are satisfied.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: The CAD 30,000 threshold is measured on a worldwide basis for all taxable supplies, including those made through digital platforms; the CRA also deems platform operators to be the supplier in certain e-commerce marketplaces.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Although no real-time clearance exists, CRA audit systems perform risk-based analytics on invoice and payment data; inconsistent BN, missing tax, or implausible export patterns increase audit selection risk.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated export treatment is available under Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act as follows: (i) tangible goods delivered to a destination outside Canada (Part V, s. 1, with the goods required to be exported as soon as reasonably possible); (ii) services supplied to a non-resident person (Part V, s. 7) where the non-resident is not a GST/HST registrant and the service is not in respect of real property situated in Canada or tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time the service is performed; and (iii) intangible personal property, including software licences and cloud/digital document-automation IP, supplied to a non-resident (Part V, s. 10) where the entitlement is not for use in Canada. For the ULC's LegalTech contract-automation and e-signature SaaS, the principal claim is zero-rating under Part V, s. 7 as a service supplied to a non-resident customer; the supply to Canadian-resident customers remains taxable at 5% GST. The supplier must hold contemporaneous records proving the non-resident status of the customer, the delivery of the digital service outside Canada, and the absence of use or enjoyment in Canada.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: B13A Export Declaration (electronic export declaration filed through the Canadian Export Reporting System, CERS) for goods exported from Canada when the value exceeds CAD 2,000
Commercial invoice and packing list identifying the supplier, buyer, description of goods, quantities, and export value
Transport evidence: bill of lading (ocean), air waybill (air), or courier/CERS e-manifest (land, rail, and express) proving that the goods physically departed Canada

Banks and inward remittance records: Inward Remittance Certificate, foreign exchange settlement, SWIFT/credit-card settlement statements evidencing receipt of consideration from the non-resident buyer

Executed SaaS subscription agreement, e-signature service order, and digital delivery logs (API records, download/IP geolocation data) demonstrating that the service was delivered to and consumed outside Canada
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Although Canada does not impose a statutory foreign-currency repatriation deadline, the 180-day benchmark is applied as an internal documentary-control and audit-readiness standard for zero-rated export claims; CRA requires export and payment evidence to be retained for six years. If CRA denies a zero-rating claim, the full 5% GST/HST becomes payable on the consideration, and CRA may reassess beyond the normal four-year reassessment period (extended to eight years where a return contains a misrepresentation, neglect, or fraud attributable to the taxpayer) and recover previously refunded net tax with prescribed daily compounded interest. Statutory penalties include: (i) a false-statement or omission penalty of the greater of CAD 100 and 50% of the net tax understated (ETA s. 280(1)) for GST/HST; (ii) a parallel gross-negligence penalty of the greater of CAD 100 and 50% of the tax sought to be avoided (Income Tax Act s. 163(2)) where the T2 return is affected; (iii) criminal prosecution for willful evasion (ETA s. 327 and ITA s. 239) with fines of up to 200% of the tax evaded and terms of imprisonment; and (iv) joint and several director liability for unremitted GST/HST, interest, and penalties under ETA s. 323. CRA audit teams scrutinize export claims for round-tripping, missing CERS declarations, absence of outward shipping evidence, FX receipt mismatches, and same-day invoice/payment patterns, and the registrant bears the burden of proof.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility_note: For a purely digital LegalTech SaaS export, no customs declaration is required; the substantiation bundle shifts to contracts, geolocation/delivery logs, customer billing addresses, and tax-residence evidence, and the 5% zero-rating applies only if the customer is a non-resident and the service is not consumed in Canada.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.mandatory_fx_repatriation_deadline_days_: The 180-day figure is a conservative documentary benchmark, not a statutory deadline; the governing limitation is the six-year record-retention obligation under ETA ss. 286-287 and the normal four-year reassessment limitation under ETA s. 296.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle_n: Where the ULC exports only intangible services (SaaS software, e-signature authentication, document automation), the 'customs bundle' is satisfied by commercial contracts, delivery logs, payment evidence, and non-resident status documentation rather than by a physical customs declaration.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada). Functional FX administration: Bank of Canada under the Currency Act and Bank of Canada Act; prudential banking supervision: Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); AML/CFT supervisor: FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA); inbound investment review: Department of Finance / Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada under the Investment Canada Act. Canada has no separate 'foreign exchange administration' agency or exchange-control licensing body.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full IMF Article VIII convertibility. Both current-account and capital-account transactions are freely convertible for CAD and foreign currency; there are no surrender, conversion-margin, licensing, or destination restrictions. The CAD has floated since 1970; the Bank of Canada intervenes only in exceptional disorderly-market conditions. Profit-remittance hurdles are tax-driven, not FX-driven: (i) Part XIII withholding tax on ULC dividends to the US parent — 25% statutory, reduced to 5% under US-Canada Income Tax Convention Article X where the US parent is a resident of the US and owns at least 10% of the ULC's voting shares; (ii) monthly CRA remittance of withheld amounts and NR4 information returns; (iii) FINTRAC/EDD reporting on cross-border electronic transfers of CAD 10,000 or more; (iv) Investment Canada Act notification once the ULC commences a new Canadian business — non-discretionary filing, with substantive net-benefit review applying only for non-WTO investors (CAD 5M direct acquisitions) or large WTO acquisitions (2024 enterprise-value threshold CAD 1.365B), both far above a LegalTech SaaS operation; (v) no government approval required for recapitalization, upstream dividends, or intercompany loan repayments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Zero surrender requirement — Canada imposes no statutory timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts. SaaS subscription revenue, software-licence royalties, and other service export proceeds may be retained indefinitely in USD, EUR, or any other currency in any jurisdiction. The only compliance triggers are: (i) physical cross-border currency movements of CAD 10,000 or more must be reported to the CBSA; (ii) electronic funds transfers of CAD 10,000 or more are reportable by banks/fintechs to FINTRAC (not by the company); (iii) for Canadian income tax, amounts are computed in CAD using Bank of Canada daily exchange rates under ITA s. 261, with an optional functional-currency election available to qualifying corporations. The ULC should adopt a written FX conversion policy for monthly CRA/GST filings, intercompany settlement, and Part XIII remittance calculations.

Operating Account + Capital Contribution / Shareholder Loan Sub-Account
Operating Account + US-Dollar Cross-Border Clearing Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Restricted — Low-to-Medium feasibility. Canada does not recognize the EU/UK 'EMI' licence. Non-bank payment service providers operating in Canada must register with FINTRAC as money-service businesses and, where regulated as retail payment activity providers, must register with the Bank of Canada under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) during the 2025 transitional registration window. An offshore EMI cannot act as the ULC's primary operating bank because it lacks access to Payments Canada's Lynx/ACH settlement rails, cannot receive CRA payroll-deduction remittances, is not CDIC-insured for CAD deposits, and will not support the MT103 SWIFT routing needed for Part XIII and intercompany transparency. Feasibility as primary banking partner: LOW. Feasibility as a supplementary cross-border payout/collection conduit (e.g., Wise Business, Payoneer, Stripe Treasury-type products): MEDIUM, strictly limited to sub-CAD 10,000 per transaction flows and never as the principal account. Stripe itself must be configured as a merchant processor settling into a Schedule I bank account in the ULC's legal name.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person branch meeting or live video interview is effectively mandatory for the ULC's authorized signatories and for the US parent's controlling officer. Tier-1 banks will generally permit remote opening where a Canadian-resident director appears at a branch with original corporate documents and the US parent's CFO joins by video with a notarized resolution, but internal credit and EDD committees typically require 15–25 business days for sanctions/OFCAC screening, beneficial-ownership verification, and product approval. Documents issued by the US (incorporation, incumbency, articles) must be apostilled under the Hague Apostille Convention, which entered into force for Canada on January 11, 2024. The ULC must maintain an Alberta registered office; the ABCA does not mandate Canadian-resident directors for a wholly-owned ULC, but the bank will ordinarily require at least one Canadian-resident director or a named Alberta agent for service of process to pass KYC. A US parent guarantee or awareness letter is a standard credit condition, and the bank will require a FATCA self-certification — Form W-9 for the ULC as a US disregarded entity or Form W-8BEN-E with the US parent's EIN, depending on the bank's interpretation of the check-the-box election.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: ULC 'unlimited liability' feature flags the vehicle as unusual or potentially a shell/holding entity; compliance may confuse the Canadian tax-transparent ULC with an unlimited liability partnership or require parent-level financial support evidence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Alberta Corporate Registry full file (Certificate of Incorporation, Articles of Amendment, Corporate Access Number, annual return); ULC by-laws and unanimous shareholders agreement; US parent's audited financial statements; Form 8832 check-the-box election certificate prepared by US tax counsel; board resolution confirming the ULC is a wholly-owned operating entity with no subsidiaries and no unsubstantiated capital; signed indemnity and creditor-notice letter to the bank quantifying the unlimited-liability exposure and confirming contractual back-stop from the US parent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident sole shareholder (US parent) and non-resident directors trigger enhanced due diligence; the bank may question economic substance, particularly if the Delaware parent appears thin or if the ULC is classified as a disregarded entity for US tax while being a corporation for Canadian tax.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: US parent Form 6166 (US residence certificate); IRS EIN and FATCA self-certification; W-8IMY/W-8BEN-E as applicable; group organogram with ultimate beneficial owners aged and verified; Alberta office lease, payroll records, and utility contracts; three-year Canadian financial projections; intercompany services and IP licence agreements supported by a transfer-pricing study under ITA s. 247; evidence that the ULC's directors have valid Canadian immigration status or that an Alberta-resident agent for service has been appointed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party payment processor (TPPP) concentration: all receivables settling through Stripe with credit-card chargebacks/refunds create unascertained floating liabilities and item-level merchant data that the bank cannot inspect.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed Stripe Merchant Agreement in the exact legal name of the ULC; PCI DSS Attestation of Compliance (SAQ-A or higher); 12-month historical processing volume and settlement ledger; chargeback ratio attestation below 0.75% and refund-rate forecast; settlement-sweep design showing all Stripe payouts denominated in CAD to the ULC's Schedule I operating account; written undertaking to notify the bank of any processor change; compliance with the Voluntary Code of Conduct for the Credit and Debit Card Industry in Canada.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small business deduction: federal 9% + Alberta 2% on first CAD 500,000 of active business income; investment tax credits; SR&ED credits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return, filed via CRA e-file or NETFILE using approved software
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 6 months after fiscal year-end; e.g., for Dec 31 year-end, due June 30 of the following year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Canadian-source revenue for non-resident corporations
Deduct expenses reasonably allocated to Canadian-source income
Compute based on Part I rules; apply treaty provisions if applicable
Apply federal rate; consider treaty relief for permanent establishment
Alberta corporate tax applies to income attributable to Alberta permanent establishment

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month up to 12 months; late payment interest at prescribed rate (currently 8% for 2025).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief, file Form NR301 (dividends) or NR302 (interest/royalties) with CRA; provide Certificate of Residence (e.g., IRS Form 6166 for US) and complete treaty-based disclosure on T2 return.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 25%, treaty 10% (US); Interest: statutory 25%, treaty 15% (US) but generally exempt if arm's length and not contingent on profits.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1 million for total transactions with non-residents (services) or CAD 5 million for other transactions; large corporations with gross revenue > CAD 50 million must prepare Master File and Local File.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not have specific ESR, but General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) and substance-over-form principles apply; CRA may challenge transactions lacking economic substance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of income or false deductions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of 50% of tax evaded, plus interest; criminal prosecution with fines up to 200% of tax evaded and imprisonment up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for unpaid corporate tax under Section 227.1 of the Income Tax Act; travel bans and asset freezes possible.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a ULC as a conduit without real business activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR reassessment, denial of treaty benefits, penalties up to 50% of tax avoided.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for negligence if they knowingly participate in sham arrangements.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to report large cash transactions or suspicious transactions under Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 500,000 for corporations; criminal penalties up to CAD 500,000 and imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally liable for penalties if they knowingly fail to comply.
